risks.title: Risk: Block legacy authentication
risks.description: MS.AAD.1.1v1 was not met in this scan (Fail). 0 conditional access policy(s) found that meet(s) all requirements.
risks.statement: The security risk of allowing legacy authentication protocols is they do not support MFA. Blocking legacy protocols reduces the impact of user credential theft.

risks.title: Risk: Block high-risk users
risks.description: MS.AAD.2.1v1 was not met in this scan (Fail). 0 conditional access policy(s) found that meet(s) all requirements.
risks.statement: Blocking high-risk users may prevent compromised accounts from accessing the tenant.

risks.title: Risk: Block high-risk sign-ins
risks.description: MS.AAD.2.3v1 was not met in this scan (Fail). 0 conditional access policy(s) found that meet(s) all requirements.
risks.statement: This prevents compromised accounts from accessing the tenant.

risks.title: Risk: Complete authentication methods migration
risks.description: MS.AAD.3.4v1 was not met in this scan (Fail). Requirement not met
risks.statement: To disable the legacy authentication methods screen for the tenant, configure the Manage Migration feature to Migration Complete. The MFA and Self-Service Password Reset (SSPR) authentication methods are both managed from a central admin page, thereby reducing administrative complexity and potential security misconfigurations.

risks.title: Risk: Disable SMS, voice call, and email OTP
risks.description: MS.AAD.3.5v2 was not met in this scan (Fail). Requirement not met
risks.statement: SMS, voice call, and email OTP are the weakest authenticators. This policy forces users to use stronger MFA methods.

risks.title: Risk: Phishing-resistant MFA for privileged roles
risks.description: MS.AAD.3.6v1 was not met in this scan (Fail). 0 conditional access policy(s) found that meet(s) all requirements.
risks.statement: This is a backup security policy to help protect privileged access to the tenant if the conditional access policy, which requires MFA for all users, is disabled or misconfigured.

risks.title: Risk: Require managed devices for authentication
risks.description: MS.AAD.3.7v1 was not met in this scan (Warning). 0 conditional access policy(s) found that meet(s) all requirements.
risks.statement: The security risk of an adversary authenticating to the tenant from their own device is reduced by requiring a managed device to authenticate. Managed devices are under the provisioning and control of the agency. [OMB-22-09](https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/M-22-09.pdf) states, "When authorizing users to access resources, agencies must consider at least one device-level signal alongside identity information about the authenticated user."

risks.title: Risk: Block device code authentication
risks.description: MS.AAD.3.9v1 was not met in this scan (Warning). 0 conditional access policy(s) found that meet(s) all requirements.
risks.statement: The device code authentication flow has been abused to compromise user accounts via phishing. Since most organizations using M365 don't need device code authentication, blocking it mitigates the risk.

risks.title: Risk: Only admins register applications
risks.description: MS.AAD.5.1v1 was not met in this scan (Fail). 1 authorization policies found that allow non-admin users to register third-party applications: authorizationPolicy
risks.statement: Application access for the tenant presents a heightened security risk compared to interactive user access because applications are typically not subject to critical security protections, such as MFA policies. Reduce risk of unauthorized users installing malicious applications into the tenant by ensuring that only specific privileged users can register applications.

risks.title: Risk: Use finer-grained roles instead of Global Administrator
risks.description: MS.AAD.7.2v1 was not met in this scan (Fail). Requirement not met: Least Privilege Score = 2 (should be 1 or less) Calculated by 2 global admins / 1 privileged users without global admin role
risks.statement: Many privileged administrative users do not need unfettered access to the tenant to perform their duties. By assigning them to roles based on least privilege, the risks associated with having their accounts compromised are reduced.

risks.title: Risk: Cloud-only accounts for privileged users
risks.description: MS.AAD.7.3v1 was not met in this scan (Fail). 1 admin(s) that are not cloud-only found: John Public
risks.statement: By provisioning cloud-only Microsoft Entra ID user accounts to privileged users, the risks associated with a compromise of on-premises federation infrastructure are reduced. It is more challenging for the adversary to pivot from the compromised environment to the cloud with privileged access.

risks.title: Risk: Provision privileged roles only through PAM
risks.description: MS.AAD.7.5v1 was not met in this scan (Fail). 3 role(s) assigned to users outside of PIM: Global Administrator, SharePoint Administrator, User Administrator
risks.statement: Provisioning users to privileged roles within a PAM system enables enforcement of numerous privileged access policies and monitoring. If privileged users are assigned directly to roles in the M365 admin center or via PowerShell outside of the context of a PAM system, a significant set of critical security capabilities are bypassed.

risks.title: Risk: Alert on privileged role assignments
risks.description: MS.AAD.7.7v1 was not met in this scan (Fail). 6 role(s) or group(s) without notification e-mail configured for role assignments found: Cloud Application Administrator(Directory Role), Exchange Administrator(Directory Role), Global Administrator(Directory Role), Hybrid Identity Administrator(Directory Role), Privileged Role Administrator(Directory Role), SharePoint Administrator(Directory Role)
risks.statement: Closely monitor assignment of the highest privileged roles for signs of compromise. Send assignment alerts to enable the security monitoring team to detect compromise attempts.

risks.title: Risk: Alert on Global Administrator activation
risks.description: MS.AAD.7.8v1 was not met in this scan (Fail). 1 role(s) or group(s) without notification e-mail configured for Global Administrator activations found: Global Administrator(Directory Role)
risks.statement: Closely monitor activation of the Global Administrator role for signs of compromise. Send activation alerts to enable the security monitoring team to detect compromise attempts.

risks.title: Risk: Alert on other privileged role activation
risks.description: MS.AAD.7.9v1 was not met in this scan (Warning). 5 role(s) or group(s) without notification e-mail configured for role activations found: Cloud Application Administrator(Directory Role), Exchange Administrator(Directory Role), Hybrid Identity Administrator(Directory Role), Privileged Role Administrator(Directory Role), SharePoint Administrator(Directory Role)
risks.statement: Closely monitor activation of high-risk roles for signs of compromise. Send activation alerts to enable the security monitoring team to detect compromise attempts. In some environments, activating privileged roles can generate a significant number of alerts.

risks.title: Risk: Limit guest access to directory objects
risks.description: MS.AAD.8.1v1 was not met in this scan (Warning). Permission level set to "Same as member users" (authorizationPolicy)
risks.statement: Limiting the amount of object information available to guest users in the tenant, reduces malicious reconnaissance exposure if a guest account is compromised or created by an adversary.

risks.title: Risk: Only Guest Inviters can invite guests
risks.description: MS.AAD.8.2v1 was not met in this scan (Warning). Permission level set to "everyone" (authorizationPolicy)
risks.statement: By only allowing an authorized group of individuals to invite external users to create accounts in the tenant, an agency can enforce a guest user account approval process, reducing the risk of unauthorized account creation.

risks.title: Risk: The standard and strict preset security policies SHALL be enabled.
risks.description: MS.DEFENDER.1.1v1 was not met in this scan (Fail). Requirement not met
risks.statement: Defender includes a large number of features and settings to protect users against threats. Using the preset security policies, administrators can help ensure all new and existing users automatically have secure defaults applied.

risks.title: Risk: Sensitive accounts SHALL be added to Defender for Office 365 protection in the strict preset security policy.
risks.description: MS.DEFENDER.1.5v1 was not met in this scan (Fail). Requirement not met
risks.statement: Unauthorized access to a sensitive account may result in greater harm than to a standard user account. Adding sensitive accounts to the strict preset security policy, with its increased protections, better mitigates their elevated risk.

risks.title: Risk: Domain impersonation protection SHOULD be added for key suppliers and partners in both the standard and strict preset policies.
risks.description: MS.DEFENDER.2.3v1 was not met in this scan (Warning). Not all partner domains are included for targeted protection in Strict or Standard policy.
risks.statement: Configuring domain impersonation protection for domains owned by important partners reduces the risk of a user being deceived by a look-alike domain. By configuring impersonation protection in both preset policies, administrators can help protect email recipients from impersonated emails, regardless of whether they are added to the standard or strict policy.

risks.title: Risk: Safe attachments SHOULD be enabled for SharePoint, OneDrive, and Microsoft Teams.
risks.description: MS.DEFENDER.3.1v1 was not met in this scan (Warning). Requirement not met
risks.statement: Clicking malicious links makes users vulnerable to attacks, and this danger is not limited to links in emails. Other Microsoft products, such as Microsoft Teams, can be used to present users with malicious links. As such, it is important to protect users on these other Microsoft products as well.

risks.title: Risk: The custom policy SHOULD be applied to Exchange, OneDrive, SharePoint, Teams chat, and Devices.
risks.description: MS.DEFENDER.4.2v1 was not met in this scan (Warning). DLP custom policy applied to the following locations: Exchange, OneDrive, SharePoint, Teams. Custom policy protecting sensitive info types NOT applied to: Devices. Devices location requires DLP for Endpoint licensing and at least one registered device. For full policy details, see the ActualValue field in the results file: ./TestResults.json
risks.statement: Unauthorized disclosures may happen through M365 services

risks.title: Risk: At a minimum, the alerts required by the CISA M365 Secure Configuration Baseline for Exchange Online SHALL be enabled.
risks.description: MS.DEFENDER.5.1v1 was not met in this scan (Fail). Requirement not met
risks.statement: Potentially malicious or service-impacting events may go undetected without a means of detecting these events. Administrators are alerted to these events when they occur, minimizing potential user or agency impact.

risks.title: Risk: Automatic forwarding to external domains SHALL be disabled.
risks.description: MS.EXO.1.1v2 was not met in this scan (Fail). 1 remote domain(s) found that allow automatic forwarding: Default
risks.statement: Adversaries can use automatic forwarding to gain

risks.title: Risk: A DMARC policy SHALL be published for every second-level domain.
risks.description: MS.EXO.4.1v1 was not met in this scan (Fail). 1 agency domain(s) found in violation: contosodemo.onmicrosoft.com. View DNS logs, #dns-logs for more details.
risks.statement: Without a DMARC policy available for each domain, recipients

risks.title: Risk: External sender warnings SHALL be implemented.
risks.description: MS.EXO.7.1v1 was not met in this scan (Fail). Requirement not met
risks.statement: Alerting users when email originates from outside their organization can encourage them to exercise increased caution, especially if an email is one they expected from an internal sender.

risks.title: Risk: The ability to create production and sandbox environments SHALL be restricted to admins.
risks.description: MS.POWERPLATFORM.1.1v1 was not met in this scan (Fail). Requirement not met
risks.statement: Users creating new Power Platform environments may inadvertently bypass data loss prevention (DLP) policy settings or misconfigure the security settings of their environment.

risks.title: Risk: Power Platform tenant isolation SHALL be enabled.
risks.description: MS.POWERPLATFORM.3.1v1 was not met in this scan (Fail). Requirement not met
risks.statement: Provides an additional tenant isolation control on top of Microsoft Entra ID tenant isolation specifically for Power Platform applications to prevent accidental or malicious cross tenant information sharing.

risks.title: Risk: The ability to create Power Pages sites SHOULD be restricted to admins.
risks.description: MS.POWERPLATFORM.5.1v1 was not met in this scan (Warning). Requirement not met
risks.statement: Users may unintentionally misconfigure their Power Pages to expose sensitive information or leave the website in a vulnerable state.

risks.title: Risk: External sharing for SharePoint SHALL be limited to "Existing guests" or "Only people in your organization".
risks.description: MS.SHAREPOINT.1.1v1 was not met in this scan (Fail). Requirement not met
risks.statement: Sharing information outside the organization via SharePoint increases the risk of unauthorized access. By limiting external sharing, administrators decrease the risk of access to information.

risks.title: Risk: File and folder default sharing scope SHALL be set to "Specific people (only the people the user specifies)".
risks.description: MS.SHAREPOINT.2.1v1 was not met in this scan (Fail). Requirement not met
risks.statement: By making the default sharing the most restrictive, administrators prevent accidentally sharing information too broadly.

risks.title: Risk: External meeting participants SHOULD NOT be enabled to request control of shared desktops or windows.
risks.description: MS.TEAMS.1.1v1 was not met in this scan (Warning). Requirement not met
risks.statement: An external participant with control of a shared screen could potentially perform unauthorized actions on the shared screen. This policy reduces that risk by removing an external participant's ability to request control. However, if an agency has a legitimate use case to grant this control, it may be done on a case-by-case basis.

risks.title: Risk: Anonymous users SHALL NOT be enabled to start meetings.
risks.description: MS.TEAMS.1.2v2 was not met in this scan (Fail). Requirement not met
risks.statement: This policy protects against anonymous users starting Microsoft Teams meetings to scrape internal contacts. The policy is beneficial for agencies that have implemented custom policies, providing flexibility for some users to automatically admit "everyone" to a Microsoft Teams meeting.

risks.title: Risk: Agencies SHOULD only allow installation of third-party apps approved by the agency.
risks.description: MS.TEAMS.5.2v2 was not met in this scan (Warning). Org-wide tenant setting (third-party apps): All - Non-compliant (should be set to None)
risks.statement: Allowing Teams integration with third-party apps can expose the agency to potential vulnerabilities present in an app not managed by the agency. By allowing only specific apps approved by the agency and blocking all others, the agency can limit its exposure to third-party app vulnerabilities.

risks.title: Risk: Agencies SHOULD only allow installation of custom apps approved by the agency.
risks.description: MS.TEAMS.5.3v2 was not met in this scan (Warning). Org-wide tenant setting (custom apps): All - Non-compliant (should be set to None)
risks.statement: Allowing Teams integration with custom apps can expose the agency to potential vulnerabilities present in an app not managed by the agency. By allowing only specific apps approved by the agency and blocking all others, the agency can limit its exposure to custom app vulnerabilities.
